title: Movement: Fighter II moves alone and counts against fleet supply
description: The engine offers Fighter II a move of its own (move 2, no capacity) and charges every fighter that no ship's capacity holds against the fleet pool of the system (fleet.rs standing_with). The movement overlay filed such fighters under cargo: it wanted a carrier, could not stage them alone, and its Fleet Supply gauge counted non-fighters only. Now they are ships with their own row, All from here loads what the carriers hold and sends the rest alone, and the gauge shows the engine's number with a warning past the limit. Before shots were taken on 80ce1bf1; after shots are regenerated by npm run screenshots -- GA.

notes.title: The engine's rule
notes.text: Fleet supply limits non-fighter ships (LRR 37.1). A fighter is charged only when it is upgraded (Fighter II) and the capacity of the ships in the system cannot hold it, after Space Dock fighter support and the ground forces in space are counted against that capacity; Naalu's Hybrid Crystal Fighter II counts half, rounded up. Base fighters are never charged because they are removed when capacity is short.

notes.title: What changed
notes.text: The movement choice's display detail fleet_supply now also carries the inputs of that sum (ships, capacity, carried, fighters, fighter_support, fighters_upgraded, fighters_half). The client adds what is staged (web/src/presentation/fleetProjection.ts) so the gauge shows the number the engine will enforce. Rules version unchanged: no engine behaviour changed.
